_strings.@@1022227af447: Homestead Property Tax Credit (general claimants) — Available to Michigan resident homeowners and renters whose homestead is in Michigan and who were a Michigan resident for at least 6 months of the year. You must own and occupy the homestead, or rent/lease it under a contract. Cannot claim if total household resources exceed $67,300, or if the homestead's taxable value exceeds $154,000 (excluding vacant farmland classified as agricultural). Renters: in most cases 23% of rent paid is treated as property tax eligible for the credit. Separate, more generous computations apply to seniors (age 65+), the blind/disabled, paraplegic/hemiplegic/quadriplegic/deaf claimants, and veterans/surviving spouses.

_strings.@@3a1936765382: Treaty conformity — MI conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from MI income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the MI return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: MI starts from federal AGI and has no treaty add-back, so federally treaty-exempt income (already excluded from federal AGI) flows through untaxed -> conforms. Confirmed two ways from michigan.gov sources: (1) The 2023 MI-1040 begins at line 10 "Adjusted Gross Income from your U.S. Form 1040," and Michigan modifications are only the enumerated additions on Schedule 1 (line 11) and subtractions (line 13). (2) The 2023 Schedule 1 "Additions to Income" lines 1-8 contain NO addition for income exempt under a federal tax treaty (the additions are: non-Michigan municipal interest/dividends, self-employment/income taxes deducted federally, MI-1040D/4797 capital gain adjustments, out-of-state business/property losses, oil/gas extraction expenses, federal NOL deduction, and MESP/MET nonqualified withdrawals). The words "treaty"/"treaties" appear zero times in the entire 2023 MI-1040 instruction booklet, so there is no Michigan add-back analogous to California's Schedule CA treaty addback.

_strings.@@6960cb6a3217: Home Heating Credit (low-income heating-cost credit) — Helps qualified low-income Michigan homeowners and renters pay part of their home heating costs. Eligibility and credit are determined by the number of exemptions and a corresponding income ceiling using a standard-allowance method (MI-1040CR-7 Table A) or an alternate computation (Table B). Claimed on a separate form, not on the MI-1040 itself. NOTE: the specific 2023 standard-allowance dollar amounts and income ceilings could not be independently confirmed from a tax-year-2023 official source in this research, so the dollar figures are left blank and flagged unverified.

_strings.@@f2b49ad48cfa: Michigan Earned Income Tax Credit for Working Families (EITC) — You must qualify for and claim the federal EITC. If you do not qualify for the federal EITC, you do not qualify for the Michigan EITC. Aimed at low-to-moderate-income working individuals and families; eligible amount depends on income, filing status, number of qualifying children, and/or disability. Beginning with tax year 2023 the rate is 30% of the federal credit (the Lowering MI Costs plan / Public Act 4 of 2023 raised it from 6% to 30%).

state_tax.work_common_tail: 0. Tax line: MI-1040 Line 17: "Tax. Multiply line 16 by 4.05% (0.0405)" (Line 16 = taxable income; Line 15 = exemption allowance; Line 10 starts from federal AGI). Verified exemption kinds shipped but NOT applied by this op (compute them on the form): disabled_veteran ($400 — Line 9c: $400 qualified disabled veteran exemption. NOT applied by calc.state_tax.); special_disabled ($3,100 — Line 9b: $3,100 special exemption — deaf, blind, hemiplegic, paraplegic, quadriplegic, or totally and permanently disabled. NOT applied by calc.state_tax.); stillbirth ($5,400 — Line 9d: $5,400 stillbirth exemption (certificate of stillbirth). NOT applied by calc.state_tax.) This op computes the state's flat-rate tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: The 4.05% rate is a ONE-YEAR statutory reduction for tax year 2023 only (the book says the rate is "reduced to 4.05%" for 2023) — never carry it to any other year. Claimed as a dependent by another: enter $0 on line 9a and $1,500 on line 9e instead of the $5,400 personal exemption — calc.state_tax does not model this; compute line 9e on the form. Michigan CITY income taxes (Detroit and other cities, e.g. Form 5118/CF-1040) are NOT modeled — calc.state_tax computes the state 4.05% line only.
